To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electron-cation complex formation in dye-sensitised ZnO nanoparticles is the main reason for the fast charge recombination in these systems.

the electron mobility in ZnO nanoparticles is strongly decreased by the presence of cations at the semiconductor surface, and the mobility can recover to its original value when the cation is removed.

(i) the electron-cation complex formed in dye-sensitised ZnO nanocrystals is a key factor in the fast charge recombination, which can be overcome by using a high permittivity material, and (ii) the electron mobility in dye sensitised ZnO nanocystals is significantly lower compared to the mobility in nonsensitised nanocrystals, due to the electron-cation interactions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of a cationic dye on the surface of a semiconductor nanocrystal has an important influence on the charge transport properties of the nanocrystal.
the electron mobility in ZnO nanoparticles is significantly reduced in the presence of dye cations due to the strong electron-cation electrostatic interaction.
the electron mobility in the dye-sensitized semiconductor nanoparticles is strongly influenced by the presence of the dye cation and its charge distribution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electron mobility of dye-sensitized semicondutors is not only determined by the intrinsic material properties but also by the electron-cation electrostatic interaction.

the electron-cation complex is the major factor responsible for fast charge recombination in ZnO-based solar cells, while the high permittivity of TiO2 efficiently screens the charges and prevents the formation of such complexes.
the electron-cation complex is not a problem for dye-sensitized TiO2, but it can be for dye-sensitised ZnO.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electron-cation complex can be a major obstacle to efficient charge transport in ZnO sensitized solar cell materials.
the electron-cation complex can be avoided by using dye molecules with a large dipole moment, which will be a promising strategy to enhance the efficiency of ZnO-based solar cells.
the electron-cation complex formation in ZnO nanoparticles is a major factor that limits charge transport and thus limits the efficiency of ZnO-based dye-sensitized cells.
